answer: Staked identity bonds make sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock collateral before it can act, and that stake is slashed when peers attest to misbehavior. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand bonds, so forged crowds cannot wander the network for free. Honest tenure lets a bond compound toward its zenith of trust, while a fresh sybil starts at the bottom of the knoll. To outvote the honest set an attacker must out-stake it, which is the whole cost.
